failures: tests (required status check, ruleset `main-protection`): FAILURE on head 60360661 — 7 failures, all in tests/automation/test_agent_invoke_wrapper.py, every one of them `CompletedProcess(... bootstrap/invoke_agent.sh ...)` exiting 1 with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'` raised at scripts/automation/agent_invoke_cli.py:61.

Root cause (verified at the line): bootstrap/invoke_agent.sh's final statement is `exec python3 "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/automation/agent_invoke_cli.py" "$@"` — a bare PATH lookup. In CI that resolves to the actions/setup-python 3.12 interpreter (.github/workflows/tests.yml:60), NOT scripts/oversight/.venv, which is where PyYAML>=6.0 is declared (scripts/oversight/requirements.txt:17). scripts/framework/run_tests.sh:75 runs pytest as "$VENV_PYTHON" -m pytest, so tests/automation/test_agent_invoke_cli.py (1,064 lines, in-process import) passes under the venv interpreter; only the 7 tests that shell out through the wrapper cross into the bare python3 and fail. The split between the two test files is the tell, and it is deterministic — pytest-rerunfailures re-ran all 7 and all 7 failed again ("7 failed, 3234 passed, 16 skipped, 7 rerun").

Scope note (this is not a CI-only environment gap): the same bare-python3 exec makes the canonical entry point fail on any host whose system python3 lacks PyYAML — including a consumer project after bootstrap/hos_install.sh, which installs no venv. It did not reproduce on the overseer's own machine because /usr/bin/python3 there happens to carry PyYAML 6.0.1; the clean CI runner is the honest environment. Note also that `yaml` is used at exactly two lines (agent_invoke_cli.py:237-238, yaml.safe_load / yaml.YAMLError on agent-file frontmatter) — whether to route the wrapper to the venv interpreter, add PyYAML to the CI test environment, or drop the dependency is the designer's call, not a constraint imposed here.
